name: Reorder
purpose: Provide accessible manual reordering for one controlled linear collection through drag, keyboard movement, and direct movement controls.
useWhen: A user deliberately controls the saved order of items in one vertical or horizontal list.

avoidWhen.condition: Items are ordered automatically by a data field, query, table header, or server sort rule.
Movement changes tree parents, table row semantics, Kanban containers, or freeform coordinates.
avoidWhen.useInstead: a component-specific adapter built on DragDrop

composition: Provide Root with stable item identities, getItemLabel, controlled onItemsChange, and one keyed Item for each identity in the same order.
Place a labelled Handle and visible MoveBefore/MoveAfter or equivalent movement controls inside every movable Item.
Optionally render DropIndicator for styled insertion feedback; keep application content and controls inside each Item.

rules.statement: Treat Root items as the canonical controlled identity order and render Items in that same order.
Provide stable identities and human getItemLabel output for instructions and announcements.
Include visible direct movement controls so the operation does not require a dragging path.
Do not combine active automatic sorting with manual reordering unless the application clearly disables or reconciles one behavior.
Keep persistence, optimistic updates, Undo, conflicts, validation, and error recovery in the application.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using the rendered index as Item value or rendering Items in an order different from Root items.
commonMistakes.correction: Use durable record IDs and render the controlled identity order exactly.

commonMistakes.mistake: Showing only a drag handle because keyboard users can also move it.
commonMistakes.correction: Keep the handle and add visible MoveBefore/MoveAfter or an equally direct simple-pointer alternative.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using Reorder to change a sorted result set while its sort remains active.
commonMistakes.correction: Disable reordering or switch the collection to a documented manual-order mode first.

validation: Verify drag, keyboard, and direct-control changes emit the same final identity order and accurate previous/next indices.
Verify boundary controls disable correctly and disabled/read-only Items cannot move.
Verify focus remains on the same keyed control after re-render, including first/last movement and RTL horizontal order.
Verify application persistence failures can be recovered without Atom owning remote state.
